answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation Form 8-K dated August 17, 2026 (Items 1.01, 2.03, 7.01) describing residual value guaranties with SB Energy for the Portsmouth Site; company-issued primary filing on a signed agreement, with forward-looking terms and conditions stated by management.

findings.claim: On August 17, 2026 NVIDIA entered into multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy as Lessor, covering leases for approximately 4.25 GW of IT load in aggregate at the Portsmouth Site (Pike County, Ohio). Each Agreement generally becomes effective only upon commencement of the applicable lease.
findings.use: Supports the limited conclusion that NVIDIA has an existing signed contingent guaranty obligation covering about 4.25 GW of leased IT load. It does not establish that any payment will be made, since effectiveness waits for lease commencement.
findings.grounds: The company is the direct party to the agreements and reports the signing as a fact on the filing date, so the existence of the signed agreements is directly reported by the obligor. The uncertainty that matters is timing: the guaranty is contingent and becomes effective only at lease commencement, so the signing does not itself create a cash outflow.
findings.next_check: The full text of the Agreements is to be filed as an exhibit to the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026. Check the exhibit for the commencement mechanics and the guaranteed minimum value per lease, which determine when and how much exposure becomes effective.

findings.claim: NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation under its initial commitment is cumulatively capped at $105 billion. Its payment obligations are subject to specified conditions, including that the Lessor has satisfied the applicable ready-for-service conditions under the lease for the relevant premises, which the filing expects to begin in 2028.
findings.use: Conditional: supports a ceiling of $105 billion on initial-commitment exposure, with actual payments dependent on lease effectiveness, ready-for-service milestones, and a trigger event. The $105 billion figure is a maximum, not an expected payment, and the 2028 timing is a company expectation.
findings.grounds: The cap and the ready-for-service condition are contractual terms stated by the obligor in its own filing, so the company can know them. The 2028 start is a forward-looking expectation of management and carries delivery risk for the Lessor's construction schedule. The key uncertainty is whether the Lessor meets ready-for-service conditions on schedule, which determines when the exposure can become payable.
findings.next_check: Compare the 10-Q exhibit's definition of the cap, the ready-for-service conditions and any timing outside conditions against later NVIDIA filings and any SB Energy or OpenAI disclosures on Portsmouth construction and power milestones.

findings.claim: NVIDIA may provide credit support to secure approximately an additional 3.8 GW at the Portsmouth Site, exercisable in its sole discretion.
findings.use: Lead: indicates a possible further expansion of NVIDIA's contingent exposure at Portsmouth, but it is an option and not a committed obligation. Whether this expansion occurs is unresolved, so it should not be treated as part of the existing commitment.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA states the option directly and it is discretionary, so the company knows the option exists. The filing gives no price, cap, or timing for this additional support, and the forward-looking expansion language in the filing makes its likelihood uncertain. The unresolved point is whether NVIDIA will exercise the option and under what terms.
findings.next_check: Watch for any NVIDIA filing or announcement that exercises the additional credit support, and for the terms of that exercise, including any cap, which would convert this option into a measurable obligation.

findings.claim: OpenAI, through an affiliate of OpenAI Group PBC, is the tenant. If OpenAI becomes insolvent and defaults under a lease, or fails to make lease payments (each a Trigger Event), NVIDIA will pay generally the shortfall between the guaranteed minimum lease value and amounts recovered through a replacement lease or sale. OpenAI has agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for amounts actually paid.
findings.use: Conditional: supports reading NVIDIA's exposure as a tenant-default guaranty, where the size of any payment depends on OpenAI's default and on the recovery through re-leasing or sale. The OpenAI indemnity is a recovery right whose value depends on OpenAI's financial capacity, which the filing does not establish.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA is a direct party to the guaranty and states its trigger and reimbursement terms, so the description of the contract mechanics is reported by the obligor. The creditworthiness of OpenAI and the value of its indemnity are not established by this filing, and the trigger depends on future events not yet observed.
findings.next_check: Check the 10-Q exhibit for the guaranteed minimum value formula and the indemnity terms. Check OpenAI's independent financial disclosures or credit assessments, to judge whether the reimbursement right is likely to be realized if a Trigger Event occurs.

findings.claim: Upon a Trigger Event NVIDIA may choose to assume the lease, require the Lessor to relet the premises, initiate a sale process, allow the lease to terminate, or defer these remedies for up to one year while paying specified project agreement costs. NVIDIA's obligations end at the earliest of the 20th anniversary of lease commencement, termination of the lease by OpenAI under its terms, OpenAI achieving a satisfactory credit rating, or other customary termination events.
findings.use: Conditional: supports reading NVIDIA's guaranty as having several remedy paths and bounded duration, which affects how a default would be absorbed. It does not establish which remedy NVIDIA would choose or what costs the deferral would involve.
findings.grounds: The remedies and termination events are contract terms that the company states as the obligor. The choice among remedies is at NVIDIA's discretion and depends on conditions in a future default, and the cost of deferral is only described as specified project agreement costs without amount in this filing.
findings.next_check: Check the 10-Q exhibit for the amount and definition of the specified project agreement costs during deferral, and for the definition of satisfactory credit rating that would end the obligation.

findings.claim: NVIDIA has secured land, power and shell capacity at the Portsmouth Site to host NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure, and OpenAI as tenant will use capacity supporting approximately 4.25 GW of IT load to deploy NVIDIA's full-stack DSX AI factory platform, subject to limited exceptions.
findings.use: Conditional: supports the announced commercial model in which the guaranteed leases are tied to a stated end-use of NVIDIA's DSX AI factory platform by OpenAI. The end-use is company-stated intent for the tenant's deployment, not an independently verified buyer commitment in this filing beyond the lease structure.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA describes the planned deployment and the tenant relationship in its own announcement, so it can know the intended use it is structuring. The filing does not report the tenant's independent commitment to the platform purchase, nor the limited exceptions. The uncertainty that matters is whether OpenAI's deployment actually proceeds as the company describes, since NVIDIA's guaranty exposure depends on that tenancy.
findings.next_check: Look for OpenAI's own disclosures or statements on the Portsmouth lease and on DSX platform deployment, and for NVIDIA's later reporting on DSX revenue or deployments at the site to confirm the stated end-use.
